structured_output.what_is_happening: PROM is a pump.fun coin created about 2h25m ago. It left the bonding curve within about 6 minutes and now trades on PumpSwap with about $28.5k of liquidity, and the LP tokens are burned. It peaked near $342k market cap (ATH price 0.000342), probably in the first hour, and did about $1.6M of volume in its first 2 hours. It then fell roughly 80%. At detection it had bounced sharply: +164% in 30 minutes and +38 to 62% in 5 minutes, to about $95k. Hourly volume has dropped to about $84k, from an average of more than $600k/h earlier. In the last hour, unique sellers (736) outnumbered unique buyers (599). The dev wallet has closed its position (creator_close). GMGN shows the coin as a community takeover with 10 paid DexScreener boosts. The coin is linked to promx.fun / @usePromX, described as 'Post about a coin. Get paid from its fees.'

narrative.description: This is a utility/platform story: a 'post-to-earn' product that shares coin fees with people who post about the coin. That fits the 2025-26 theme of pump.fun creator-fee sharing. The story is somewhat coherent, but it is the platform's token, not a meme with broad cultural pull. The launch pattern looks like a hyped product launch: very high early volume, a fast migration, then a sharp fall.
narrative.why_spreading: The early spike was probably product-launch hype and possibly the platform's own incentive loop. The current move looks like a dead-cat bounce after an ~80% fall, supported by paid boosts and a community-takeover (CTO) relaunch of the profile. None of this shows fresh organic demand.

token_connection.why_this_token: This is the only same-ticker pair with real liquidity and volume. It carries the project's website and X link, and it was created first among the burst of PROM clones that appeared the same morning.
token_connection.competing_tokens: At least 7 PROM clones were launched within minutes to hours of this one. All show zero liquidity and zero volume, and some show fake-looking market caps ($997k, $285k). There is also an unrelated older PROM (Prom, $67M, a bridged asset). The clone swarm means the launch drew copycats.

authenticity.evidence: The spread of holders is real: about 5k holders and 5.2k unique buyers over 6h, top-10 holders at about 18%, and no insiders flagged. On the other side, GMGN tags 550 wallets as bundlers and 1,000 as fresh wallets, and bot/degen activity is at 43%. There are 10 paid boosts, the coin is a CTO, and the dev has exited. 40 smart wallets and 2 KOL wallets touched it, but the smart-money signal count is 0.
authenticity.uncertainty: Without X data I can't tell whether @usePromX has real users or whether the platform is still pushing the coin. The bundler count may also reflect early launch snipes that have already sold out.

structural_risks: Heavy overhead supply: to reach the target (~$190k+) price has to climb back toward holders who bought near the $342k ATH
Volume is falling fast (h1 is about 1/7 of the 6h hourly average), and sellers outnumber buyers in the last hour
The entry comes 25 minutes after a +164% bounce in 30 minutes, so the risk is buying at the local top
The dev has exited and the coin is a CTO, so the team's commitment is unclear
The bundler and fresh-wallet share is high
The LP is burned, so a classic liquidity pull is unlikely, but the pair can still die from lack of volume

structured_output.counterargument: The coin has a real product with a working website and a mechanism, 'get paid for posting', that pushes holders to shill it. Its ATH of $342k shows demand was there, and about 5k holders is a large base for a $95k coin. The LP is burned, so it can't be rugged by a liquidity pull. A CTO with paid boosts after a deep correction is a classic setup for a second leg. From $95k, a return to $190k is only about 55% of the prior ATH. If the platform goes live or a KOL posts about it, a 2x within 6 hours is plausible.

structured_output.thesis: This is a launch-hype platform token that peaked at about $342k and is now bouncing from about $40k to $95k on paid boosts after a CTO. Volume is decaying and sellers outnumber buyers. The most likely outcomes are that the bounce fades or the price drifts down toward the stop. A second leg to 2x is possible given the product narrative and the holder base, but it is not the base case. Because the LP is burned, a hard rug is unlikely; the more likely failure is a slow death.
